clue.text: To snooze in the course of it is unseemly

indicators.note: something happening in the course of another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written
to snooze is to nap

explanation.surface: Someone declares that dozing off during something is bad manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe behaviour that is inappropriate or out of place in the circumstances.

clue.text: Native American with something to add when success comes late?

parts.note: an older term for an indigenous American is Indian
read cryptically, a summer is one that adds or totals figures

explanation.surface: An indigenous American has more to say about late achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase also means a spell of warm weather in autumn, so a late flowering in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a late period of happiness or achievement in someone's life, after the expected time.

clue.text: Stunned in vehicle after a stitch-up

indicators.note: the vehicle comes after the other pieces
in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to stitch is to sew
a truck is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone sits dazed in a van after being framed.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'stitch-up' is British slang for being framed, but here it is SEW turned 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overwhelmed with wonder or fear is to be stunned, a close synonym.

clue.text: Fighter at one time stony broke

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former boxer ended up penniless, stony broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stony broke' is British slang for penniless; 'broke' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Tyson was a heavyweight boxing champion, now retired, so a former fighter.

clue.text: Gangster seldom seen pocketing note

indicators.note: one piece pockets another by holding it inside itself

parts.note: something seldom seen is scarce
fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A rarely spotted mobster tucks away a banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarface was the nickname of Al Capone and the title of famous films about a mob boss.

clue.text: Second eleven cricketer bagging duck — an old 20, perhaps

parts.note: a cricket or football eleven is a team

indicators.note: bagging means holding inside

parts.note: a bat is a batsman, a cricketer
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A reserve cricketer is out for nothing, a cricket score of zero.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is the answer at 20-down, a word for a cargo ship without a fixed route; an old one would be steam-powered.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam-driven vessel was the old kind of tramp steamer, so an example of the other entry.

clue.text: Lying president finally exposed

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of exposed

explanation.surface: A dishonest head of state is at last found out.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying here means lying down, in bed, not telling untruths.

clue.text: In fancy, prepares to fight alien over ranch

indicators.note: In puts the following pieces inside fancy

parts.note: a fad is a passing fancy
to arm is to prepare for fighting

indicators.note: in a down clue, over signals turning the word upward, backwards

parts.note: ET is the film extra-terrestrial, an alien

explanation.surface: A fantasy in which a cattle ranch gears up to battle a space invader.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm with its buildings is a homestead, and a ranch is a large farm.

clue.text: Trainer has nothing in reserve — energy's lacking

indicators.note: lacking means the letter is missing
in places nothing inside the reserve

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store or reserve
O is zero, nothing
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A sports trainer has no spare players and his side is tired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts O into CACHE for COACHE, and 'lacking' drops E.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports instructor who trains athletes is called a coach.

clue.text: Players' last practice session covered up

definitions.meaning: the final run-through by actors before opening night, in costume
cryptically, a rehearsal done while dressed, that is, clothed

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: a rehearsal performed fully clothed is literally 'covered up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors hold a full costumed run-through just before the first performance, and the costumes are what cover them.

clue.text: Space traveller's walks occur amid high tension

indicators.note: amid means set among, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: HT is the abbreviation for high tension
alleys are walks or paths
to come is to occur, as in thoughts that come

explanation.surface: A tense high-voltage moment as a spacewalk takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous periodic body that orbits the sun every 76 years, a traveller through space.

clue.text: Many initially opted out in conflict for independence

indicators.note: words in conflict are at odds and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged
initially points to the opening letter of opted

explanation.surface: Many people chose to leave during a war in order to gain their freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes only O from 'opted'; with MANY and OUT that gives eight letters for 'in conflict' to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-government or freedom from outside control is what both words describe.

clue.text: Complaint from Queen on street hemmed in by motorists

indicators.note: to be hemmed in by something is to be surrounded by it, so these pieces sit inside

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is placed after it

parts.note: HM stands for Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A monarch out on a road gets boxed in by drivers and develops a breathing problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint here is an illness or ailment, and this is a chronic respiratory condition.

clue.text: Kicks up a fuss as channel's about to go

parts.note: a sound is a sea channel, and the 's adds an S
food about to go bad is off, as is an event about to start

explanation.surface: Someone complains loudly because a TV station is closing down.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean to complain or protest loudly and at length.

clue.text: O'Connor, left out of pursuit, removing unwanted coat

parts.note: Des O'Connor was a British TV entertainer and singer

indicators.note: one letter comes out of the word

parts.note: a calling is a pursuit or vocation

explanation.surface: A singer leaves his job and sheds a layer of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing limescale from a kettle or a fish's scales strips away an unwanted layer.

clue.text: I'm surprised about vote cutting money reserved for dogs

indicators.note: cutting means splitting the word open and going inside

parts.note: funds are money set aside

indicators.note: about here means round the outside, so the exclamation encloses the vote mark

parts.note: oho is an exclamation of surprise
X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a ballot that slashes money set aside for animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts X in OHO for OXHO, which 'cutting' places in FUNDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting hounds bred to chase a particular quarry are a type of dog.

clue.text: Skinned bass displayed in fish stand

indicators.note: something displayed in another piece is set inside it

parts.note: an eel is a fish

indicators.note: a skinned word loses its outer letters, keeping only its middle

explanation.surface: A filleted bass sits on show among other fish at a market stall.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's frame stand holds a canvas or board upright, so it is a stand.

clue.text: Before half-time, still bagging good place for big game

indicators.note: the first piece is placed before the second
bagging means holding inside

parts.note: serene means calm and still

indicators.note: half of the word means its first two letters

explanation.surface: A football side, calm ahead of the interval, snaps up a fine result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big game' looks like a major match but means large wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tanzanian national park is famous for its large wild animals, so a home for them.

clue.text: Forces join around a thousand in retreat

indicators.note: going backwards, so the built word is read in reverse
one piece goes around another, enclosing it

parts.note: a seam is a join between pieces of fabric
K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: Military units link up around a thousand troops while falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' puts K inside SEAM to give SEKAM, which 'in retreat' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To force someone to do something is to compel them, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Revised dietary mix omitting one type of stuffing

indicators.note: a revised version is reworked, so these letters are rearranged
omitting means leaving something out

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A nutrition plan is altered, dropping one kind of meal filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Omitting' removes one I from DIETARYMIX; 'Revised' rearranges the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Preparing and mounting animal skins involves filling them, a jokey kind of stuffing unlike the culinary one.

clue.text: Catch parent in a flustered state

indicators.note: flustered suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child catches a mother or father looking flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch someone out with a trick is to snare or trap them.

clue.text: Constituent pinches money raised for march

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read bottom to top
pinches means holding tightly inside

parts.note: a part is a constituent

explanation.surface: A voter steals cash that was collected for a protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinches' puts M in PART for PMART, which 'raised' reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge or walk heavily over a long distance is to march.

clue.text: Book about leaders of note in conurbation like St Helens

parts.note: VOL is short for volume, a book
CA, for circa, means about

indicators.note: leaders of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A book about prominent local musicians from the English town of St Helens.
explanation.walkthrough: St Helens is a town near Liverpool, but the definition means Mount St Helens, the volcano in Washington state.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount St Helens is a volcano that erupted in 1980, so it is of that fiery mountain type.

clue.text: Endless succession of agency clerks

indicators.note: of signals the letters are taken out of these words

explanation.surface: A never-ending stream of temp office workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeating round of events that keeps coming back is a recurring series.

clue.text: Stop distress becoming audible

indicators.note: becoming audible means as heard when spoken

parts.note: woe is distress or misery

explanation.surface: An order to halt as someone's misery starts to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: An instruction to halt, especially to a horse, is a command to stop.

clue.text: Cosmetic effect of brain drain?

definitions.meaning: a skin preparation that disappears when rubbed in
a brain drain sees the best people, the cream, disappear abroad

explanation.walkthrough: Cream also means the elite, so in a brain drain the cream is vanishing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a face lotion that soaks into the skin and seems to disappear, a beauty product.

clue.text: It helped Nelson see grand plays produced on board

indicators.note: being on board a ship puts a piece inside the steamship letters

parts.note: on board means inside SS, the steamship abbreviation

indicators.note: plays produced are put on in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Plays are staged aboard a ship, which Admiral Nelson could watch.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson famously put a telescope to his blind eye at Copenhagen so as not to see a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hand telescope is the instrument a naval officer like Nelson used to see distant ships.

clue.text: Are spades imported to make tracks?

indicators.note: something imported is brought inside

parts.note: to make tracks is to leave, to exit
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: A question about whether shovels are brought in to lay a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: To be is to have being or reality, so 'are' in the plural means the same as live or be present.
